⚡️Filipino scientists have detected elevated nuclear isotopes in the West Philippine Sea.

⚡️Researchers found iodine-129, a long-lived radioactive isotope, in seawater samples.

⚡️119 samples analyzed showed concentrations 1.5–1.7 times higher than nearby regions.

⚡️Iodine-129 is not natural — it is a byproduct of nuclear fission, indicating human nuclear activity.

⚡️Experts confirm no immediate threat to public health or marine ecosystems.

⚡️Traces were likely carried by ocean currents from the Yellow Sea.

⚡️The source is linked to nuclear fuel reprocessing and historical weapons testing in northeastern China.

The study highlights how interconnected global oceans are.
